message.content: The core risk here is numerical: the one-pass variance in float32 with mean≈64 will suffer catastrophic cancellation against a float64 reference with only 2% tolerance. I'll record that as the primary in-scope claim, plus the mean-error variant.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "total is a sequential float32 sum of 128 values each ~64, giving mean error ~1e-5–1e-4 absolute; since deviations x[i]-mean are only ~0.125, relative error in the numerator is ~1e-3–1e-2 per element, systematic across the vector and potentially stacked with the variance error to breach 0.02.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "The contract defines reference[i] = (x[i]-mean)/sqrt(var+1e-5) with float64 evaluation and tolerance rel-L2 <= 0.02 on exactly this workload; since deviations are ~0.125, mean precision directly controls numerator accuracy."}], "statement": "The float32 sequential accumulation of `total` (sum of 128 values ~64) yields a mean with absolute error ~1e-5–1e-4, which is comparable to the per-element deviations (x[i]-mean ~ 0.125) at the ~0.1% level and, combined with denominator error, may push the relative L2 error over the 0.02 limit even if the variance itself survives cancellation."}

message.reasoning_content: Record the key claims: one-pass float32 variance cancellation exceeding 0.02 rel L2 on this fixed workload; mean accumulation error also amplified. Maybe one claim suffices plus clamp-to-zero as subcase. Record 2 claims.
